title: He Shot a Newsweek Cover and Lost the Copyright
excerpt: Lester LaRue shot a Newsweek cover on the morning of the Oklahoma City bombing, then lost the copyright to his employer. The court ruled the photos were works made for hire, and the lesson for every working photographer is that ownership is settled before the shutter, not after.

title: A Spinning Fan Stood Still on Camera. That Is a Lesson in Shutter Speed
excerpt: A YouTuber froze a spinning fan on video by matching its speed to his camera's frame rate. The trick is a clean, watchable lesson in what frame rate and shutter speed each actually control, and why video of spinning things cannot be trusted at face value.

title: Camera Prices Could Rise in 2027. Buy on a Plan, Not on a Panic.
excerpt: Canon told investors it no longer expects memory prices to fall in 2027, and will raise camera prices if costs stay high. That is a reason to make your next purchase decision now, not to rush one.
